Overseas, the war in Ukraine took an ugly civilian turn.

Russia battered Kyiv and the surrounding region for a fifth straight night, and this time it went after food warehouses — NPR and the Kyiv Independent both describe bare supermarket shelves across the capital, hit by a wave of jet-powered drones that are faster and harder to shoot down.

Ukraine's air defense still knocked out ninety-six of a hundred and twenty-one drones overnight, but six people were hurt.

The squeeze is aimed at everyday life now, not just the grid.

Next door to Israel, quieter friction worth a mention.

Israel is openly frustrated that Lebanon's army is moving too slowly to disarm Hezbollah in the south, while a US official notes that Lebanese officers actually don't want Israeli troops pulling out yet — they're worried Hezbollah simply walks back in the moment they leave.

The ceasefire is holding, but it's clearly fragile.

On the science front, something to chew on — literally.

A new study flags that two of the most common zero-calorie sweeteners, sucralose and stevia, may reshape your gut in ways that outlast the sweet taste, with early hints the effect can even carry across generations.

It's preliminary and mostly animal work, so don't go panic-tossing the protein powder — but it's one to keep half an eye on.

On tech, two things.

First, a small but real date for a builder like you: Anthropic's introductory pricing on Claude Sonnet five ran out at midnight, so from today it's back to standard rates — three dollars per million tokens in, fifteen out.

If you're wiring it into anything, that cheap-trial window has quietly closed.

Clear skies, essentially no rain, just a light northeasterly breeze — nothing to plan around.

Word of the day: saudade — a deep, bittersweet longing for someone or something you love and that's now absent.

As in, one glance at old competition photos and the saudade hits.

And an AI tip: when you actually need facts, tell the model straight out that it's allowed to say "I don't know" — giving it permission to be uncertain cuts right down on those confident, made-up answers.
